🗳️ In-person voting began this Saturday in Mexico for the elections on the 29th, with moderate turnout and complaints about delays in mailing ballots. 📊 A total of 192,306 Spanish citizens are eligible to vote in Mexico: 140,464 in Mexico City, about 37,000 in Monterrey, and just over 12,000 in Guadalajara. 📍 In Mexico City, the polling station at the Hospital Español will remain open until Thursday, the 26th, at 6:30 p.m. local time (12:30 a.m. GMT on Friday). ⚖️ Uncertainty persists regarding the votes of those naturalized under the “Grandchildren’s Law.” 📉 The consulate expects voter turnout to be around 6% or 7% of registered voters.
